newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-STEWART HITS FIRST CENTURY OF NZ TOUR.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-STEWART HITS FIRST CENTURY OF NZ TOUR.

text.p: PALMERSTON NORTH, New Zealand, (Reuter) Jan 15 - Alec Stewart kept up his excellent form with the bat on Wednesday by completing the first century of England's cricket tour to New Zealand against a selection XI.
Stewart began day three of the four-day fixture on 75, with England at 154 for three wickets in reply to the New Zealand side's first innings 138.
He moved smoothly to his century when he cut fast-medium Robert Kennedy to the backward point fence and then hooked the next ball for a single to fine leg.
Stewart's 38th first-class century had taken 206 minutes, came off 168 balls and included 14 boundaries.

International cricket's top test scorer in 1996 with 793 runs, Stewart also stood out as a class batsman in the recent tour of Zimbabwe, where the England team humiliated itself with a poor overall showing.
He made 105 against a President's XI in a one-day match in Zimbabwe and hit an unbeaten 101 in the second test.
Together with Nasser Hussain, Stewart had pushed England into a commanding position in its first tour match in New Zealand.

By lunch England had advanced to 240 for three wickets, with Stewart on 127 and Hussain on 39. The pair's unbroken fourth wicket stand was worth 134 runs and England had amassed a first innings lead of 102 with seven wickets standing.
